issues.detail: The Greek 'πιασας αυτον της δεξιας χειρος' (took him by the right hand) is rendered as 'nắm tay hữu' (took/held the right hand), which misses the object 'αυτον' (him). The Vietnamese implies holding a hand, whereas the Greek specifies taking *him* by the hand.

The Greek 'ηγειρεν' means 'raising/lifting up'. The Vietnamese 'đỡ dậy' (supporting/lifting up) is acceptable, but the phrase 'người nắm tay hữu người đỡ dậy' suggests two different people performing two different actions, whereas the Greek structure implies a single action of taking him by the right hand to raise him.
